newsitem.title: FRANCE: French officials decline comment on Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: French officials decline comment on Thomson-CSF.

text.p: French officials declined comment on Tuesday on newspaper reports that the government had decided to sell defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF through a private placement rather than a public offer.
The government is due to announce its plans for the sale of Thomson-CSF before the end of the month.
Financial dailies Les Echos and La Tribune said on Tuesday the sale would be through a private sale, following up a similar report in afternoon daily Le Monde on Monday.
Officials at Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office and the finance and industry ministries all declined comment on the reports.
Thomson-CSF is 58 percent held by Thomson SA, which is wholly owned by the state. Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere Groupe are interested in acquiring Thomson-CSF.
The government stated its preference in October for an offer from Lagardere for Thomson SA, which also owns consumer electronics firm Thomson Multimedia (TMM), over a rival bid from Alcatel.

Lagardere had teamed up with South Korea's Daewoo Electronics but the government cancelled the procedure in December after the independent Privatisation Commission said it could not approve the terms of the deal.
It announced afterwards that it would sell its Thomson-CSF stake and TMM separately.
Alcatel has boosted its position by lining up Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation for a joint bid.
